considered_not_taken.why: a second model scores completion from the transcript (complete when its score reaches 1.0); a model verdict is not a receipt. Its one transferable rule, an unreadable verdict means keep working, is already implied by judging from parsed runner output. The empty-patch critic (empty_patch.py, sha256 fdfbd5abbec31727bd852e6f0287546b5e0b302cc6f15ae136aa36da32c9efb6) is the core's 'an empty diff is not a fix', which diffaudit.py exits 2 on.

its error log, never-repeat-a-failing-action rule and three-strike escalation match what SWE-agent, Aider and the core already give; its stop gate judges a phase-status marker in the plan file, which this skill rejects as a completion oracle; three planning files in the project would be the scratch this skill forbids. Its stall rule (no ledger progress since the last block allows the stop) agrees with the no-progress stop taken from Qwen.

its strongest idea, re-run core passing checks before new work in a fresh session, is already in the core's handoff.md and build.md resume steps (inherited, not re-taken); the agent flips a passes field with no receipt, which this skill treats as a claim.

the living plan with recorded discoveries and a restart-from-the-plan test is the core's task record and handoff note (inherited); the instruction not to ask the user about next steps conflicts with the authority rules; a full plan document belongs to westack-plan.

a host checklist tool with at most one step in progress (plan_tool.rs, sha256 0a5482699b191fbeeb8f58790b62f6b331b64e29a38b3286a669aff4c699fdd9, and update_plan_instructions.rs, sha256 9bd837cc7760dc670ba7454f251a2a039b3d5a5e2bc6e16b916c9d400393337b, also read): a progress view the host already provides, not evidence; nothing for a skill to carry.

a mandatory clarifying-question phase and three competing architecture designs suit an unapproved feature, not an authorised change; build asks only questions whose answer changes the work. 'Read the files explorers name' is the core's inspect rule.
its trivial-work route and its care with files that were already dirty agree with what fatstack and the core give; the rest is an engine-selection and shipping workflow outside build.

rejected as a completion oracle (core decision D18): the loop ends when the model's last message contains the promise text, and max_iterations defaults to unlimited. Its session-id isolation of the state file is noted for a future host adapter; this skill installs no hook.

diffaudit.py: one deterministic pass over saved git output for scope, deferred execution, weakened tests, narrowed test selection, scratch and pre-existing dirty paths

helper_decision.reason: Four of this skill's rules are claims about the delivered diff (scope, deferred execution, tests not weakened, no scratch) that an agent otherwise checks by eye at the end of a long session, which is when it is least reliable. A standard-library pass over saved git output turns them into one deterministic report, never runs a command, and also serves westack-verify's delivery diff audit. The loop judge needed no new script: the core's checks.py parse and diff already decide it.
helper_decision.tests: tests/test_diffaudit.py: 25 tests, red against a stub first (24 failing on behaviour, none on import), then green; two broken-copy mutants (skip detection off, scope check off) each fail the tests that name them
